subject.title: Anaheim Elementary School District Board, Trustee Area 4

text: It has been an honor serving as a special education classroom teacher for almost a decade, supporting student literacy and math skills. Living and working in Anaheim, I see the needs of our community's students first-hand and collaborate with families daily to support their success. I have attended nearly every board meeting for almost two years, providing public comment. My priorities include:

Leadership: I commit to holding district leaders to high standards and compliance with the law. In September 2025, the District Attorney's Office investigated a possible Brown Act violation, California's open meeting law, regarding the board's voting process. AESD then spent thousands of dollars on attorneys and re-voted to ratify the entire agenda. The board also compensated trustees who didn't attend meetings with a stipend without approving a resolution, in violation of AESD's own bylaws and education code. Any board member found to have been paid in error should repay the district. Any board member or employee who the district pays to attend a conference, but fails to do so, should reimburse the district. Our limited tax dollars should be spent on classroom instruction and infrastructure.

Transparency and Access: Government must be accountable to the people it serves. I support sharing taxpayer-funded survey results publicly and allowing community members who work long hours to provide public comment, even if arriving after a board meeting starts. All stakeholders should receive notice of district town hall meetings, including taxpayers who may not currently have children in the district. Holding regular community coffee chats and meetings with stakeholders is a must for responsiveness, gathering input, and resolving complaints before they escalate.

Fiscal Stewardship: I opposed the February board vote of a 300% raise, to $24,000 per year, while holding only one meeting per month. There should be offsetting revenue or budget savings to justify this expense. AESD should eliminate Trustee healthcare benefits and establish travel budgets. Trustees don't need full-time benefits or unlimited travel, especially during these financial times. We need school-run kitchens for local control and quality student meals. Textbooks need review for cost-efficiency, accessibility for our diverse student populations, and supplemental use to the expertise of our teachers’ instruction.

I would be honored to earn your vote to advocate for innovative and effective policies that benefit our students and community. I am available via phone, text, or email: (657) 201-7520 and lopez4schoolboard@gmail.com. Thank you.
